claims.text: A controlled yttrium microaddition will promote formation of a coherent, adherent alumina scale on CoNiCrAlY-based HEA bond coats.
The yttrium-induced alumina scale will improve bond-coat durability and reliability during high-temperature oxidation.
Precise alloying or calibrated post-deposition surface doping can produce a uniform yttrium distribution.
The intervention should remain effective during oxidation at approximately 1200–1300°C for at least 200 hours.
Yttrium addition produces an yttrium-enriched alumina scale at the oxide/bond-coat interface.
The yttrium-enriched alumina scale has enhanced adhesion and reduced defect evolution.
At high temperature, yttrium atoms segregate to grain boundaries in the growing alumina scale.
Yttrium segregation reduces alumina grain-boundary mobility.
Yttrium segregation reduces void formation in the alumina scale.
Reduced grain-boundary mobility and void formation minimize defect nucleation and oxide spallation.
Yttrium-modified samples will exhibit slower oxidation kinetics than untreated bond coats.
Yttrium-modified samples will exhibit less spallation and greater mechanical integrity than untreated bond coats.
Untreated HEA bond coats typically form less coherent and more defect-prone alumina scales during high-temperature oxidation.
There is an optimal yttrium dosage range for improving oxide-scale performance.
Insufficient yttrium provides inadequate scale enhancement, whereas excessive yttrium can form undesirable phases and degrade performance.

contradictions.description: The stated starting material is CoNiCrAlY, whose designation already includes yttrium, but it is also described as lacking reactive-element modification or yttrium addition and is to be modified by introducing yttrium.

The boundary explicitly predicts that excessive yttrium may cause detrimental phases and degraded performance, while the falsification rule treats detrimental behavior at higher yttrium levels as falsifying the hypothesis. That result is therefore both predicted and designated as a falsifier.
